title: Phase 3: Implement OIDC device-code login (toppy login)
description:
## Goal
Implement `toppy login` using OIDC device-code flow to acquire a short-lived token for gateway auth.

## Scope
- Add minimal OIDC device-code client (no browser dependency beyond printing URL/code).
- Cache token on disk (configurable path) and refresh if supported.
- Wire `toppy doctor`/`toppy up` to resolve token via cache when auth.mode=oidc_device_code.

## Acceptance
- `toppy login` succeeds against a mock IdP (tests).
- Token cache read/write is covered by unit tests.
- `toppy up`/`doctor` can run with auth.mode=oidc_device_code without manually setting auth_token.

title: Refactor gateway CONNECT-UDP handling into per-stream tasks
description: Refactor gateway CONNECT-UDP handling so each accepted request stream is serviced independently and future UDP work has a stable base.
design: Split auth, request classification, and relay handling; the main goal is per-stream isolation.
acceptance_criteria: Per-stream servicing exists; healthz, ping, echo, forward, and auth still work.
notes: Test viewpoint: exercise more than one CONNECT-UDP stream without interference.

title: Phase 3: Apply rate limiting to session traffic
description:
## Goal
Apply token-bucket rate limiting to actual traffic paths to reduce abuse.

## Scope
- Identify where `toppy-core::rate::TokenBucket` exists and wire it into data path.
- Add config knobs (burst/rate) with safe defaults.
- Add tests that assert throttling behavior.

## Acceptance
- Rate limiting is enforced in at least one real traffic path.
- Unit tests validate throttling and configuration parsing.

title: CONNECT-UDP: CLI UDP proxy
description:
Implement user-facing UDP proxying over MASQUE CONNECT-UDP (beyond doctor echo).

Background:
- Doctor already verifies connect-udp handshake and HTTP Datagram echo.
- Next step is a CLI that can forward UDP traffic for real apps (DoQ/games/etc).

Acceptance criteria:
- New CLI command (name TBD: toppy udp or toppy udp-proxy) can forward UDP to an allowed target.
- Respects existing policy rules and returns a clear denial reason.
- Has basic integration test (can be limited to loopback) and runs in CI.
- Docs updated in README/spec.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLI: `toppy udp` or `toppy udp-proxy` adds UDP forwarding to a specific target.
- Enforces existing `[policy]` allow rules; denied targets fail fast with reason.
- Works against `toppy-gw` over CONNECT-UDP; not limited to doctor echo.
- Includes at least one integration test runnable in CI (loopback is acceptable).
- README/spec updated with usage and config.

title: Bind auth subject into audit records and shipping path
description: Extend the audit pipeline so access decisions and sessions can be attributed to the resolved auth subject and preserved through shipping and verification.
design: Thread a normalized subject identity through audit event creation rather than duplicating provider-specific fields at each call site.
acceptance_criteria: Audit events can include the resolved auth subject; subject attribution survives local verification and remote shipping; missing subject data is handled explicitly; tamper-evident behavior is preserved.
notes: Test viewpoint: add verification coverage for subject-bearing records and one shipping-path check if practical.

title: Phase 3: Windows Wintun support (TUN)
description:
## Goal
Support TUN interface creation on Windows via Wintun.

## Scope
- Evaluate Wintun dependency strategy (bundled DLL vs system install).
- Implement minimal adapter creation and teardown.
- Extend `toppy doctor` with Windows TUN permission check.

## Acceptance
- `toppy doctor` reports tun.perm meaningfully on Windows.
- A minimal integration test strategy is documented.

title: Windows Wintun packaging and docs
description:
Improve Windows support around Wintun.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clear docs for placing wintun.dll and env vars.
- CI or manual test guidance that validates doctor tun check.
- If feasible: package sidecar layout for releases.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document Wintun DLL placement and env vars (`TOPPY_WINTUN_DLL`, `TOPPY_WINTUN_DIR`, etc.).
- Provide CI or manual test guidance validating `toppy doctor` tun check.
- If feasible, define a release sidecar layout for `wintun.dll`.

title: Add UDP peer idle cleanup and stream caps
description: Add idle cleanup and explicit active peer and stream caps so UDP state cannot grow without bound.
design: Define ownership for peer maps and timestamps first, then add cleanup and cap enforcement around that model.
acceptance_criteria: Idle state is reclaimed after a defined timeout; caps exist for active peers or streams; limit behavior is explicit; active traffic is not broken.
notes: Test viewpoint: cover idle expiry, cap enforcement, and continued traffic for active peers.

title: Audit log hardening and shipping
description:
Make audit logging tamper-evident end-to-end and easier to operate.

Background:
- Hash-chained JSONL writer/verify exists; CLI logs some events.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ensure key CLI actions consistently write audit events.
- Add optional signing or remote shipping target (design + minimal implementation).
- Document operational guidance and threat model implications.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ensure key CLI actions write audit events consistently.
- Add design + minimal implementation for signing or remote shipping.
- Document operational guidance and threat model implications.
- Include tests for audit verify and any new format/transport logic.

title: Apply token bucket rate limiting to CONNECT-UDP datagrams
description: Apply the existing token bucket to CONNECT-UDP datagrams so UDP traffic has explicit backpressure and abuse controls.
design: Integrate limiting at the datagram boundary so it composes with later cleanup and metrics work.
acceptance_criteria: Rate limiting exists on the UDP data path; scope is documented; exceed behavior is observable; low-rate traffic still works.
notes: Test viewpoint: add unit coverage and an integration case for throttling.

title: Add Windows CI job for Wintun doctor check
description: Add a Windows CI job that downloads or stages wintun.dll, sets TOPPY_WINTUN_DLL or TOPPY_WINTUN_DIR, runs 'toppy doctor --json', and asserts tun.perm=pass. This completes the Windows TUN integration test coverage mentioned in README.

title: Phase 3: Audit log tamper-proof application
description:
## Goal
Apply the existing hash-chain JSONL writer/verify (in `toppy-core::audit`) to actual audit log emission and verification flows.

## Implementation
- Identify where audit logs are currently written (CLI + GW).
- Wire in chained writer so each event links to previous hash.
- Add `toppy audit verify` (or equivalent) to validate the local log.
- Decide on keying/seed strategy (local-only first; remote later).

## Acceptance
- A modified/edited JSONL entry is detected by verify.
- Unit tests cover writer + verifier integration.
notes: Wired audit hash-chain into CLI flows (doctor/up) and added  (uses TOPPY_AUDIT_LOG / config.audit_log_path / default path). Added helper append_event + tests and ensured audit writer creates parent dirs.

title: Dev setup: install Rust toolchain (cargo/rustup)
description:
## Goal
Ensure contributors can run `make fmt/clippy/test` locally.

## Context
In this environment `cargo`/`rustup` are not present, so quality gates can't be executed.

## Work
- Add a minimal dev-setup section to README with commands for macOS/Linux/Windows.
- Add a `make bootstrap` target that checks for `cargo` and prints actionable install instructions (no auto-install).

## Acceptance
- `make bootstrap` prints clear guidance when `cargo` is missing.
- README has a concise “Dev setup” section.
notes:
Added ERROR: cargo not found.

Install Rust (stable) via rustup:
  macOS/Linux:
    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
    source /Users/akira/.cargo/env
  Windows:
    https://rustup.rs/ (download rustup-init.exe)

Then re-run:
  make fmt clippy test to detect missing cargo and print rustup install steps; documented Dev setup in README.

title: Remove nested legacy workspace and de-duplicate repo entrypoints
description: The repository still contains a nested toppy workspace snapshot with its own Cargo manifest and docs. Remove or archive it so the repo has one canonical workspace root and one authoritative set of entrypoint docs.
design: Prefer removing the duplicate tree entirely if it is obsolete. If anything must be preserved, move it under an explicitly archival path and document that it is not active.
acceptance_criteria: The repository has a single authoritative workspace root; stale nested manifests and docs are removed or clearly archived; README and spec references point to the canonical workspace; CI and local cargo commands still run from the root without path ambiguity.
notes: Test viewpoint: verify cargo metadata and cargo test --workspace from the repo root; spot-check README and spec commands.

title: Add CLI/GW UDP metrics and visibility
description: Expose active peer counts, stream counts, drops, and throttle signals so UDP behavior can be observed without packet captures.
design: Prefer a small explicit metrics surface aligned with cleanup and rate-limit concepts rather than verbose debug spam.
acceptance_criteria: Key UDP counters are exposed intentionally; output distinguishes normal traffic from cleanup or throttling; the signal is usable in local debugging and CI logs.
notes: Test viewpoint: add targeted tests for counters or reports and verify one integration path surfaces the new signals.

title: IdP expansion beyond device-code
description:
Support additional IdP patterns without breaking CLI UX.

Scope ideas:
- Improve SAML broker mode ergonomics (naming, docs, cache paths).
- Consider adding browser-based auth-code+PKCE as an alternative to device-code for desktop users.
- Clarify token refresh and expiry handling in CLI flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Written design note covering supported flows and config shape.
- At least one incremental implementation with tests.
- README/spec updated.
acceptance_criteria:
- Provide a design note describing supported auth flows and config schema.
- Clarify token caching, refresh, expiry behavior.
- Implement at least one incremental improvement with tests.
- README/spec updated accordingly.

title: Fix up --once data relay path
description: toppy up --once opens the outbound socket but does not relay application bytes. Make the one-shot mode perform real bidirectional relay and exit after that single session completes.
design: Reuse the normal proxy path instead of maintaining a special branch that only connects. Keep the change narrow to CLI forwarding logic and add a regression test for once mode.
acceptance_criteria: Bidirectional relay works for a single accepted connection; outbound connect and relay setup failures return non-zero exit status; non-once behavior stays unchanged; audit success and failure paths remain consistent.
notes: Test viewpoint: send bytes through up --once and verify end-to-end relay; run cargo test --workspace.

title: Phase 3: IdP expansion (SAML/MFA/FIDO2)
description:
## Goal
Broaden IdP support beyond current assumptions while keeping CLI UX stable.

## Scope
- Decide supported IdPs/auth mechanisms for next milestone (SAML, MFA, FIDO2).
- Define CLI flows and config surface.
- Add minimal integration stubs and docs.

## Acceptance
- Clear decision + doc for supported flows.
- Skeleton implementation with tests for parsing/config/flow selection.

title: Extend policy engine with auth subject and JWT claims
description: Extend policy evaluation beyond destination IP and port so it can use authenticated subject identity and selected JWT or OIDC claims.
design: Keep the engine provider-agnostic and pass only explicit identity inputs rather than raw token blobs.
acceptance_criteria: Policy inputs include authenticated subject identity; selected claims can affect allow or deny decisions; deny reasons stay clear; existing IP and port policies remain supported or have a documented migration path.
notes: Test viewpoint: add unit tests for claim and subject based decisions and keep existing policy tests passing.

title: Phase 3: CONNECT-UDP (MASQUE) spike
description:
## Goal
Add a path toward CONNECT-UDP support so UDP apps can traverse the tunnel.

## Scope (spike)
- Confirm what subset we want first: Extended CONNECT with `:protocol=connect-udp` and HTTP Datagrams.
- Prototype protocol encode/decode in `toppy-proto` (varint context id + payload) if not already present.
- Gateway: accept CONNECT-UDP and provide a simple datagram echo.
- CLI doctor: add checks like `masque.connect_udp` and `masque.connect_udp.datagram`.

## Acceptance
- Doctor can report pass/fail for CONNECT-UDP handshake and datagram echo.
- Integration test runs in CI (compose + doctor).
notes: Integration gate now asserts doctor CONNECT-UDP checks pass (masque.connect_udp + masque.connect_udp.datagram). GW already accepts CONNECT-UDP and echoes HTTP Datagrams; core doctor already implements handshake+echo checks.

title: Rate limiting: expand beyond TCP forwarder
description:
Rate limiting is currently applied to the CLI TCP forwarder (toppy up). Track follow-ups for applying the same concept to future MASQUE data paths and documenting tuning guidance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Document current rate limiter behavior and defaults.
- Add TODO hooks/design for applying limiter to future tunnel transports.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document current `toppy up` rate limiting behavior and defaults.
- Add design hooks/TODOs for applying rate limiting to future MASQUE/tunnel transports.
- Keep configuration shape stable (`[rate] bytes_per_sec`, `burst_bytes`).

title: S5: Windows RDP E2E reachability check
description:
## Context
Add Windows runner E2E coverage for RDP port (3389) similar to existing Linux TCP reachability checks. This is currently documented as a TODO in `TODO.md` (S5).

## Implementation
- Ensure CI job can be triggered via `workflow_dispatch` with input `rdp_host`.
- Use `scripts/e2e-rdp.ps1` with `TOPPY_E2E_RDP_HOST` (or workflow input) to run:
  - allow: start `toppy up --target <rdp_host>:3389` and verify local listener accepts TCP
  - deny: `toppy up --target <rdp_host>:3390` fails with policy deny and no listener
- Capture logs/artifacts so failures are diagnosable.

## Acceptance
- allow path succeeds (TCP connect to local forwarded port)
- deny path fails with policy deny and local port is not open
- doctor reports `policy.denied` as `fail` and includes reason in summary
notes: Implemented Windows RDP E2E: resolves hostname->IPv4, verifies allowed --once exit, checks policy.denied summary includes reason, uploads artifacts from CI.

title: Docs: audit logs are now tamper-evident
description:
## Goal
Update docs to reflect that audit logs are implemented and tamper-evident, and document `toppy audit verify`.

## Acceptance
- README includes audit log location/config and verify command.
- Makefile has a convenience target for verify (optional).
notes: Updated README with audit log docs and verify usage; added Makefile  target.

title: Phase 3: SAML strategy (broker/federation) + config wiring
description:
## Goal
Support SAML-backed enterprise IdPs without breaking CLI UX.

## Scope
- Decide approach: direct SAML vs SAML->OIDC broker/federation.
- Document recommended setup and how it maps to Toppy auth (JWT/OIDC).
- If feasible, add minimal verification logic (e.g., JWT claims mapping) in core/gw.

## Acceptance
- Clear doc of the chosen approach + example config.
- If implemented: unit tests cover config parsing and selected auth flow behavior.
